title: VegaChart.tsx crashes under SSR due to module-scope expressionFunction registration

complexity.rationale: Root cause is fully confirmed, single file, single site, and the fix (guard the registration to browser-only execution) is a well-understood, small change with no remaining research.

summary: VegaChart.tsx registers a Vega expression function at module load time, which throws when any SSR framework server-renders the initial HTML for a chart component — even as an ordinary client component, unrelated to whether the consumer is using React Server Components at all.
symptom: Any SSR framework (confirmed with Next.js App Router) throws 'expressionFunction is not a function' when server-rendering the initial HTML for a page using this library's Chart component, even when it's used as a completely ordinary "use client" component with no RSC-specific usage. Consumers must wrap the chart in next/dynamic({ ssr: false }) (or equivalent) to avoid this, but have no way to know that until they hit the crash.
rootCause: packages/react-spectrum-charts-s2/src/VegaChart.tsx registers the rscContainerWidth Vega expression function via a module-scope call to expressionFunction(...) (line 30) — a side effect evaluated during Node's server-side module evaluation, not gated to browser-only execution. Confirmed s1 has no equivalent: packages/react-spectrum-charts/src/VegaChart.tsx has no expressionFunction call anywhere, and packages/vega-spec-builder/src doesn't reference rscContainerWidth or CHART_SIZE_BREAKPOINTS at all — the responsive chart-size-breakpoint feature this expression function supports is s2-only, so this bug is s2-only too.

crossCutting.notes: requiresS1S2Parity is false — confirmed directly, not assumed: s1's VegaChart.tsx has no expressionFunction call, and vega-spec-builder doesn't use rscContainerWidth/CHART_SIZE_BREAKPOINTS anywhere. This is purely an s2 chart-size-responsiveness feature and its associated bug.

implementationPlan.change: Fixed. Wrapped the expressionFunction('rscContainerWidth', ...) registration in `if (typeof window !== 'undefined') { ... }`. jsdom (used by this file's tests) provides `window`, so the function still registers under Jest.

No test changes required — existing `rscContainerWidth expression function` tests continue to pass unmodified since jsdom provides `window`. A Jest-level 'require with no window' regression test was attempted and dropped: VegaChart.tsx's own import chain (useDebugSpec -> the '../utils' barrel -> the '../components' barrel -> EmptyState -> @react-aria/utils) hits an unrelated, pre-existing `window` reference at import time in a plain Node require, independent of this fix and present on main today. The real verification is the Next.js diagnostic below, since a bundler resolves this differently than a raw Jest require() would.

openQuestions: A second, unrelated SSR hazard exists in the same file's import chain (VegaChart.tsx -> useDebugSpec -> '../utils' barrel -> '../components' barrel -> EmptyState -> @react-aria/utils's window reference at import time). Not fixed here — confirmed not to affect the real Next.js SSR pattern (bundler resolution differs from a raw Node require), but would affect any consumer trying to require() this module outside a bundler. Worth its own follow-up if that scenario matters to a consumer.
